Beta-blockers.recommendation: Beta-blockers are recommended in ACS patients with LVEF ≤40% regardless of HF symptoms (Class I, A). Routine beta-blockers for all ACS patients regardless of LVEF should be considered (Class IIa, B).

RAAS system inhibitors.ACE inhibitors: Angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors are recommended in ACS patients with HF symptoms, LVEF ≤40%, diabetes, hypertension, and/or CKD (Class I, A). Routine ACE inhibitors for all ACS patients regardless of LVEF should be considered (Class IIa, A).
RAAS system inhibitors.Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists: Recommended in ACS patients with an LVEF ≤40% and HF or diabetes (Class I, A).

Adherence to medication.polypill: A polypill should be considered as an option to improve adherence and outcomes in secondary prevention after ACS (Class IIa, B).

Imaging.LVEF reassessment: In patients with pre-discharge LVEF ≤40%, repeat evaluation of LVEF 6–12 weeks after an ACS (and after complete revascularization and optimal medical therapy) is recommended to assess need for primary-prevention ICD implantation (Class I, C).
Imaging.Cardiac MRI: Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging should be considered as an adjunctive imaging modality to assess the potential need for primary-prevention ICD implantation (Class IIa, C).

Vaccination.Influenza: Influenza vaccination is recommended for all ACS patients (Class I, A).

Associated Conditions: Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) with heart failure symptoms
Consideration for all ACS patients regardless of LVEF
